verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्तः स बीभत्सुर्मातुलेन परंतप। दुर्मना दीनवदनो वसुदेवमुवाचह॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said, That scorcher of enemies, viz., Bibhatsu, thus addressed by his maternal uncle, replied, with great cheerlessness of heart, to Vasudeva who was equally cheerless, saying, 'O uncle, I ma unable to look at this Earth when she is reft of that hero of Vrishni' rare and those my other kinsmen.

verses.sanskrit: नाहं वृष्णिप्रवीरेण बन्धुभिश्चैव मातुल। विहीनां पृथिवीं द्रष्टुं शक्यामीह कथञ्चन॥२॥
राजा च भीमसेनश्च सहदेवश्च पांडवः। नकुलो याज्ञसेनी च षडेकमनसो वयम्॥३॥
verses.english: The king and Bhimasena and Sahadeva and Nakula and Yajnaseni, are of the same mind with myself in this matter.

verses.sanskrit: राज्ञः सङ्क्रमणे चापि कालोऽयं वर्तते ध्रुवम्। तमिमं विद्धि सम्प्राप्तं कालं कालविदां वर॥४॥
verses.english: The time has come for the departure of the king also. Know this that the hour of our departure too is near. You are the foremost of those who are well conversant with the course of time.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वथा वृष्णिदारास्तु बालं वृद्धं तथैव च। नयिष्ये परिगृह्याहमिन्द्रप्रस्थमरिन्दम॥५॥
verses.english: I shall, however, O chastiser of enemies, first remove to Indraprastha the women of the Vrishni race as also the children and the aged.'

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा दारुकमिदं वाक्यमाह धनञ्जयः। अमात्यान्वृष्णिवीराणां द्रष्टुमिच्छामि मा चिरम्॥६॥
verses.english: Having said so to his uncle, Arjuna, next addressed Daruka, saying, I wish to see forthwith the chief officers of the Vrishni heroes.

verses.sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं सुधर्मां यादवीं सभाम्। प्रविवेशार्जुनः शूरः शोचमानो महारथान्॥७॥
तमासनगतं तत्र सर्वाः प्रकृतयस्तथा। ब्राह्मणा नैगमास्तत्र परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥८॥
verses.english: When he had taken his seat here, all the citizens, including the Brahmanas, and all the ministers of state, came and stood surrounding him.

verses.sanskrit: तान्दीनमनसः सर्वान्विमूढान्गतचेतसः। उवाचेदं वचः काले पार्थो दीनतरस्तथा॥९॥
verses.english: Then Partha, more grieved than they, addressed those grieving and cheerless citizens and officers who were more dead than alive, and said these words which were well suited to the occasion.

verses.sanskrit: शक्रप्रस्थमहं नेष्ये वृष्ण्यन्धकजनं स्वयम्। इदं तु नगरं सर्वं समुद्रः प्लावयिष्यति॥१०॥
verses.english: I shall take away with me the remnants of the Vrishnis and the Andhakas! The sea will soon engulf this city.

verses.sanskrit: सज्जीकुरुत यानानि रत्नानि विविधानि च। वज्रोऽयं भवतां राजा शक्रप्रस्थे भविष्यति॥११॥
verses.english: Equip all your cars and place on them all your riches. This Vajra will be your king at Shakraprastha.

verses.sanskrit: सप्तमे दिवसे चैव रवौ विमल उद्गते। बहिर्वत्स्यामहे सर्वे सज्जीभवत मा चिरम्॥१२॥
इत्युक्तास्तेन ते सर्वे पार्थेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। सज्जमाशु ततश्चकुः स्वसिद्ध्यर्थं समुत्सुकाः॥१३॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by Pritha's son of Pure deeds, all of them hastened their preparations with eagerness for securing their safety.

verses.sanskrit: तां रात्रिमवसत्पार्थः केशवस्य निवेशन। महता शोकमोहेन सहसाऽभिपरिप्लुतः॥१४॥
verses.english: Arjuna passed that night in the palaces of Keshava. He was suddenly overwhelmed with great sorrow and stupefaction.

verses.sanskrit: श्वोभूतेऽथ ततः शौरिर्वसुदेवः प्रतापवान्। युक्त्वाऽऽत्मानं महातेजा जगाम गतिमुत्तमाम्॥१५॥
verses.english: When morning dawned, Vasudeva of great energy and prowess attained, through the help of Yoga, to the highest end.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शब्दो महानासीद्वसुदेवनिवेशने। दारुणः क्रोशतीनां च रुदतीनां च योषिताम्॥१६॥
verses.english: A loud and heart-rendering sound of wailing was heard in Vasudeva's palace, uttered by the weeping ladies.

verses.sanskrit: प्रकीर्णमूर्धजाः सर्वा विमुक्ताभरणस्रजः। उरांसि पाणिभिर्घ्नंत्यो व्यलपन्करुणं स्त्रियः॥१७॥
verses.english: They were seen with disheveled hair and divested of ornaments and garlands Beating their breasts with their hands, the indulged in heart-rendering lamentations.

verses.sanskrit: तं देवकी च भद्रा च रोहिणी मदिरा  तथा। अन्वारोहंत च तदा भर्तारं योषितां वराः॥१८॥
verses.english: Those foremost of women, viz., Devaki and Bhadra and Rohini and Madira threw themselves on the bodies of threw themselves on the bodies of their lord.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शौरिं नृयुक्तेन बहुमूल्येन भारत। यानेन महता पार्थो बहिर्निष्क्रामयत्तदा॥१९॥
तमन्वयुस्तत्र तत्र दुःखशोकसमन्विताः। द्वारकावासिनः सर्वे पौरजानपदा हिताः॥२०॥
verses.english: It was followed by all the citizens of Dwraka and the people of the provinces all of whom greatly stricken with grief, had been disposed towards the deceased hero.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याश्वमेधिकं छत्रं दीप्यमानाश्च पावकाः। पुरस्तात्तस्य यानस्य याजकाश्च ततो ययुः॥२१॥
verses.english: Before that vehicle were born the umbrella which had been held over his head at the conclusion of the horse-sacrifice he had performed while living and also the burning fires he had daily adored, with the priests who had used to attend to them.

verses.sanskrit: अनुजग्मुश्च तं वीरं देव्यस्ता वै स्वलङ्कृताः। स्त्रीसहस्रैः परिवृता वधूभिश्च सहस्रशः॥२२॥
यस्तु देशः प्रियस्तस्य जीवतोऽभून्महात्मनः। तत्रैनमुपसङ्कल्प्य पितृमेधं प्रचक्रिरे॥२३॥
verses.english: The last rites were then performed at that spot which he liked while he was alive

verses.sanskrit: तं चिताग्निगतं वीरं शूरपुत्रं वराङ्गनाः। ततोऽन्वारुरुहुः पत्न्यश्चतस्रः पतिलोकगाः॥२४॥
verses.english: The four wives of that heroic son of Shura ascended the funeral pyre and were consumed with the body of their husband. All of them attained to those happy regions which were his.

verses.sanskrit: तं वै चतसृभिः स्त्रीभिरन्वितं पाण्डुनन्दनः। अदाहयच्चन्दनेश्च गन्धैरुच्चावचैरपि॥२५॥
verses.english: The son of Pandu burnt the body of his uncle together with those four wives of his, using various kinds of scents and perfumed wood.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रादुरभूच्छब्दः समिद्धस्य विभावसोः। सामगानां च निर्घोषो नराणां रुदतामपि॥२६॥
verses.english: As the funeral pyre blazed up, a loud sound was heard of the burning wood and other combustible materials, along with the clear chant of Samans and the lamentation of the citizens and others who saw the rite.

verses.sanskrit: ततो वज्रप्रधानास्ते वृष्ण्यन्धककुमारकाः। सर्वे चैवोदकं चक्रुः स्त्रियश्चैव महात्मनः॥२७॥
verses.english: After it was all over, the boys of the Vrishnis and Andhaka races, headed by Vajra, as also the ladies, offered oblations of water to the great hero.

verses.sanskrit: अलुप्तधर्मस्तं धर्मं कारयित्वा स फाल्गुनः। जगाम वृष्णयो यत्र विनष्टा भरतर्षभ॥२८॥
verses.english: Phalguna, who was careful in observing every duty having caused this duty to be performed, went. O chief of Bharata's race, next to the place where the Vrishnis were killed.

verses.sanskrit: स तान्दृष्ट्वा निपतितान्कदने भृशदुःखितः। बभूवातीव कौरव्यः प्राप्तकालं चकार ह॥२९॥
यथा प्रधानतश्चैव चक्रे सर्वास्तथा क्रियाः। ये हता ब्रह्मशापेन मुसलैरेरकोद्भवैः॥३०॥
verses.english: The last rites were performed, according to the order of seniority, to the bodies of those heroes killed by the iron bolts born, by virtue of the curse denounced by the Brahmanas, of the blades of Eraka grass.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शरीरे रामस्य वासुदेवस्य चोभयोः। अन्विष्य दाहयामास पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः॥३१॥
verses.english: Searching out the bodies then of Rama and Vasudeva, Arjuna caused them to be burnt by expert persons.

verses.sanskrit: स तेषां विधिवत्कृत्वा प्रेतकार्याणि पांडवः। सप्तमे दिवसे प्रायाद्रथमारुह्य सत्वरः॥३२॥
verses.english: The son of Pandu, having next perforined duly those rites that are done to the manes of the dead, quickly started on the seventh day, mounting on his car.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वयुक्तै रथैश्चापि गोखरोष्ट्रयुतैरपि। स्त्रियस्ता वृष्णिवीराणां रुदत्यः शोककर्शिताः॥३३॥
verses.english: The windows of the Vrishni heroes wailing aloud, followed the great son of Pandu, viz., Dhananjaya, on cars drawn by bullocks and mules and camels.

verses.sanskrit: अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं पाण्डुपुत्रं धनञ्जयम्। भृत्याश्चान्धकवृष्णीनां सादिनो रथिनश्च ये॥३४॥
verses.english: All were in deep sorrow. The servants of the Vrishnis, their horsemen, and their carwarriors too, followed the procession.

verses.sanskrit: वीरहीनं वृद्धबालं पौरजानपदास्तथा। ययुस्ते परिवार्याथ कलत्रं पार्थशासनात्॥३५॥
verses.english: The citizens and the inhabitants of the country, at the command of Pritha's son, started at the same time and proceeded, surrounding that cavalcade destitute of heroes and numbering only women and the aged and the children.

verses.sanskrit: कुञ्जरैश्च गजारोहा ययुः शैलनिभैस्तथा। सपादरक्षैः संयुक्ताः सान्तरायुधिका ययुः॥३६॥
verses.english: The warriors who fought from the backs of elephants proceeded on elephants as huge as hills. The infanty also set out, together with the reserves.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्राश्चान्धकवृष्णीनां सर्वे पार्थमनुव्रताः। ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राश्चैव महाधनाः॥३७॥
verses.english: The children of the Andhaka, and the Vrishni races, all followed Arjuna. The Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, and rich Shudras, started keeping before them the sixteen thousand women who had formed Vasudeva's harem and Vajra, the grandson of the intelligent Krishna.

verses.sanskrit: दश षट् च सहस्राणि वासुदेवावरोधनम्। पुरस्कृत्य ययुर्वज्रं पौत्रं कृष्णस्य धीमतः॥३८॥
बहूनि च सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकस्त्रीणां हतनाथानि निर्ययुः॥३९॥
verses.english: The widows of the other heroes of the Bhoja, the Vrishni and the Andhaka races, lordless now, that started with Arjuna, numbered many millions.

verses.sanskrit: तत्सागरसमप्रख्यं वृष्णिचक्रं महर्धिमत्। उवाह रथिनां श्रेष्ठः पार्थः परपुरञ्जयः॥४०॥
verses.english: That foremost of car-warriors, that conqueror of hostile towns viz., the son of Pritha, escorted this huge procession of Vrishnis, which still abounded with wealth, and which looked like a veritable ocean.

verses.sanskrit: निर्याते तु जने तस्मिन्सागरो मकरालयः। द्वारकां रत्नसम्पूर्णां जलेनाप्लावयत्तदा॥४१॥
verses.english: After all the people had started, the ocean, the home of sharks, and alligators, flooded Dwraka, which still teemed with riches of every kind, with its waters.

verses.sanskrit: यद्यद्धि पुरुषव्याघ्रो भूमेस्तस्या व्यमुञ्चत। तत्तत्सम्प्लावयामास सलिलेन स सागरः॥४२॥
verses.english: Whatever portion of the ground was passed over, ocean immediately flooded over with his waters.

verses.sanskrit: तदद्भुतमभिप्रेक्ष्य द्वारकावासिनो जनाः। तूर्णात्तूर्णतरं जग्मुरहो दैवमिति ब्रुवन्॥४३॥
verses.english: Seeing this wonderful spectacle, the inhabitants of Dwraka walked faster and faster, saying. Wonderful is the course of fate.'

verses.sanskrit: काननेषु च रम्येषु पर्वतेषु नदीषु च। निवसन्नानयामास वृष्णिदारान् धनञ्जयः॥४४॥
verses.english: Dhananjaya, after abandoning Dwraka, proceeded by slow marches, causing the Vrishni women to rest in charming forests and mountain and by the sides of delightful rivers.

verses.sanskrit: स पञ्चनदमासाद्य धीमानतिसमृद्धिमत्। देशे गोपशुधान्याढ्ये निवासमकरोप्रभुः॥४५॥
verses.english: Arrived at the country of the five waters, the powerful Dhananjaya encamped in the midst of a land that abounded with corn and kine and other animals.

verses.sanskrit: ततो लोभः समभवद्दस्यूनां निहतेश्वराः। दृष्ट्वा स्त्रियो नीयमानाः पार्थेनैकेन भारत॥४६॥
verses.english: Seeing those widows escorted by Pritha's son alone, O Bharata, the robbers felt a great temptation.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ते पापकर्माणो लोभोपहतचेतसः। आभीरा मन्त्रयामासुः सामात्याः शुभदर्शनाः॥४७॥
अयमेकोऽर्जुनो धन्वी वृद्धबालं हतेश्वरम्। नयत्यस्मानतिक्रम्य योधाश्चेमेहतौजसः॥४८॥
verses.english: They said, 'Here there is only one bowman, viz., Arjuna. The party consists of children and the old. He escorts them alone. The warriors (of the Vrishnis) are without energy.

verses.sanskrit: ततो यष्टिप्रहरणा दस्यवस्ते सहस्रशः। अभ्यधावन्त वृष्णीनां तं जनं लोप्त्रहारिणः॥४९॥
महता सिंहनादे नत्रासयन्तः पृथग्जनम्। अभिपेतुर्वधार्थं ते कालपर्यायचोदिताः॥५०॥
verses.english: Urged by the perverse course of time, they fell upon that party, frightening it will loud leonine shouts and desirous of slaughter.

verses.sanskrit: ततो निवृत्तः कौन्तेयः सहसा सपदानुगः। उवाच तान्महाबाहुरर्जुनः प्रहसन्निव॥५१॥
verses.english: The son of Kunti, suddenly ceasing to advance along the path, turned, with his followers, towards the place where the robbers had attacked the party. Smiling the while, that mighty-armed warrior addressed the assailants, saying. “You sinful wretches, stop, if you love your lives! You will rue this when I cut your bodies with my arrows and take your lives.'

verses.sanskrit: निवर्तध्वमधर्मज्ञा यदि जीवितुमिच्छथ। इदानीं शरनिर्भिन्नाः शोचध्वं निहता मया॥५२॥
तथोक्तास्तेन वीरेण कदर्थीकृत्य तद्वचः। अभिपेतुर्जनं मूढा वार्यमाणाः पुनः पुनः॥५३॥
ततोऽर्जुनो धनुर्दिव्यं गाण्डीवमजरं महत्। आरोपयितुमारेभे यत्नादिव कथञ्चन॥५४॥
verses.english: Then Arjuna tried to string his large, indestructible, celestial bow with some effort.

verses.sanskrit: चकार सज्जं कृच्छ्रेण सम्भ्रमे तुमुले सति। चिंतयामास शस्त्राणि न च सस्मार तान्यपि॥५५॥
verses.english: He succeeded with great difficulty in stringing it, when the battle had become furious. He then began to think of his celestial weapons but they would not come to his mind.

verses.sanskrit: वैकृत्यं तन्महदृष्ट्वा भुजवीर्यं तथा युधि। दिव्यानां च महास्त्राणां विनाशाद्व्रिडितोऽभवत्॥५६॥
verses.english: Seeing that furious battle, the loss of the might of his arm, and the non appearance of his celestial weapons, Arjuna became greatly ashamed.

verses.sanskrit: वृष्णियोधाश्च ते सर्वे गजाश्वरथयोधिनः। न शेकुरावर्तयितुं ह्रियमाणं च तं जनम्॥५७॥
verses.english: The Vrishni warriors including the infantry, the elephant-warriors, and the car-men, failed to rescue those Vrishni women who were being snatched away by the robbers.

verses.sanskrit: कलत्रस्य बहुत्त्वाद्धि सम्पतत्सु ततस्ततः। प्रयत्नमकरोत्पार्थो जनस्य परिरक्षणे॥५८॥
verses.english: The concourse was very large. The robbers attacked it, at different points. Arjuna tried his best to protect it, but could not succeed.

verses.sanskrit: मिषतां सर्वयोधानां ततस्ताः प्रमदोत्तमाः। समन्ततोऽवकृष्यन्त कामाच्चान्याः प्रवव्रजुः॥५९॥
verses.english: Before the eyes of all the warriors, many foremost of ladies were dragged away, while others went away with the robbers of their own accord.

verses.sanskrit: ततो गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तैः शरैः पार्थो धनञ्जयः। जघान दस्यून्सोद्वेगो वृष्णिभृत्यैः सहस्रशः॥६०॥
verses.english: The powerful Arjuna, supported by the servants of the Vrishnis, struck the robbers with arrows shot off Gandiva.

verses.sanskrit: क्षणेन तस्य ते राजन्क्षयं जग्मुरजिह्मगाः। अक्षया हि पुरा भूत्वा क्षीणाः क्षतजभोजनाः॥६१॥
स शरक्षयमासाद्य दुःखशोकसमाहतः। धनुष्कोट्या तदा दस्यूनवधीत्पाकशासनिः॥६२॥
verses.english: Finding his arrows exhausted, he became deeply afflicted with grief. The son of Indra then began to strike the robbers with the horns of his bow.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेक्षतस्त्वेव पार्थस्य वृष्ण्यन्धकवरस्त्रियः। जग्मुरादाय ते म्लेच्छाः समन्ताज्जनमेजय॥६३॥
verses.english: Those Mlechcchas, however, O Janamejaya, in the very sight of Partha, retreated, taking away with the many foremost ladies of the Vrishnis and Andhakas.

verses.sanskrit: धनञ्जयस्तु दैवं तन्मनसाऽचिन्तयत्प्रभुः। दुःखशोकसमाविष्टो निःश्वासपरमोऽभवत्॥६४॥
verses.english: The powerful Dhananjaya considered it all as the work of destiny. Filled with sorrow he breathed heavy sights, at the thought of the non-appearance of his (celestial) weapons, the loss of the might of his arms, the refusal of his bow to obey him; and the exhaustion of his arrows.

verses.sanskrit: अस्त्राणां च प्रणाशेन बाहुवीर्यस्य संशयात्। धनुषश्चाविधेयत्वाच्छराणां संक्षयेण च॥६५॥
बभूव विमनाः पार्थो दैवमित्यनुचिंतयन्। न्यवर्तत ततो राजन्नेदमस्तीति चाब्रवीत्॥६६॥
verses.english: Considering it all as the work of destiny, he became greatly cheerless. He then ceased, O king, to make further efforts, saying, he had not the power which he had before.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शेषं समादाय कलत्रस्य महामतिः। हृतभूयिष्ठरत्नस्य कुरुक्षेत्रमवातरत्॥६७॥
एवं कलत्रमानीय वृष्णीनां हृतशेषितम्। न्यवेशयत कौरव्यस्तत्र तत्र धनञ्जयः॥६८॥
verses.english: Thus bringing with him the remnant of the Vrishnis, Dhananjaya established them at different places.

verses.sanskrit: हार्दिक्यतनयं पार्थो नगरं मार्तिकावतम्। भोजराजकलत्रं च हृतशेषं नरोत्तमः॥६९॥
ततो वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च स्त्रियश्चादाय पाण्डव। वीरैर्विहीनान् सर्वांस्तान् शक्रप्रस्थे न्यवेशयत्॥७०॥
verses.english: Escorting the remainder, with children and old men, and women, the son of Pandu established them, who were reft of heroes, in the city of Indraprastha.

verses.sanskrit: यौयुधानिं सरस्वत्यां पुत्रं सात्यकिनः प्रियम्। न्यवेशयत धर्मात्मा वृद्धबालपुरस्कृतम्॥७१॥
इन्द्रप्रस्थे ददौ राज्यं वज्राय परवीरहा। वज्रेणाक्रूरदारास्तु वार्यमाणाः प्रवव्रजुः॥७२॥
रुक्मिणी त्वथ गान्धारी शैब्या हैमवतीत्यपि। देवी जाम्बवती चैव विविशुर्जातवेदसम्॥७३॥
सत्यभामा तथैवान्या देव्यः कृष्णस्य सम्मताः। वनं प्रविविशू राजंस्तापस्ये कृतनिश्चयाः॥७४॥
द्वारकावासिनो ये तु पुरुषाः पार्थमभ्ययुः। यथार्हं संविभज्यैनान्वज्रे पर्यददज्जयः॥७५॥
स तत्कृत्वा प्राप्तकालं बाष्पेणापिहितोऽर्जुनः। कृष्णद्वैपायनं व्यासं ददर्शासीनमाश्रमे॥७६॥
verses.english: Having done all these acts suited to the occasion. Arjuna, with eyes bathed in tears, then entered the hermitage of Vyasa. There he saw the Dvaipayana seated at his ease.
